'''''Medicago rigidula''''', the '''Tifton burclover''', is a species of annual herb in the family [[Fabaceae]].

== Description ==
''Medicago rigidula'' is an [[annual plant]] with a self-supporting growth form that can grow to {{Convert|0.5|m|ft|frac=2}} tall.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tifton burclover - Encyclopedia of Life |url=https://eol.org/pages/703649 |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=eol.org}}</ref> It has compound,<ref name="go botany">{{cite web |title=Medicago rigidula — Tifton medick |url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/medicago/rigidula/ |website=Go Botany: Native Plant Trust |access-date=12 April 2022}}</ref> broad leaves.

[[File:Medicago rigidula Y01.jpg|thumb|Flower and foliage]]

Blooming in March and April,<ref name="Kew Science" /> the flower is yellow and bilaterally symmetrical. The flowers can consist of four [[petal]]s, [[tepal]]s, and [[sepal]]s, or five petals, tepals, and sepals. The petals are often between {{convert|2 and 7|mm|frac=16}} in length. Within the flower, there is a [[superior ovary]] and a [[hypanthium]]. The hypanthium provides a cup-like enlargement of the flower and surrounds the fruits.<ref name="go botany" />

[[File:Meri3 001 lhp.jpg|thumb| Fruit close-up]]

The fruit is a spiral coiled [[legume]] with a single [[carpel]] that dries but does not split open when ripe. The fruits have hairs on them and are protected with thornlike defense structures. <ref name="go botany" /> The hairs on the fruits aid in [[seed dispersal]] by adhering to the fur and feathers of various animals.

== Taxonomy ==
It is a wild relative of cultivated ''[[Medicago truncatula|M. truncatula]]'' (barrel clover) and ''[[Alfalfa|M. sativa]]'' (alfalfa).<ref name="iucn" />

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species has a widespread range occurring at elevations between sea level and {{Convert|1,800|m|abbr=on}} above sea level.<ref name="iucn" /> It is native to Albania, Algeria, Baleares, Bulgaria, Corse, Egypt, France, Greece, Italy, Kriti, Krym, Lebanon-Syria, Libya, Morocco, Palestine, Portugal, Romania, Sardegna, Sicilia, South European Russi, Spain, Tunisia, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, and Yugoslavia.<ref name="iucn" /><ref name="Kew Science" />

It has been introduced to Czechoslovakia, Great Britain, Hungary, and the US state of California.<ref name="iucn" /><ref name="Kew Science">{{Cite web |title=Medicago rigidula : Plants of the World Online - Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:20011853-1 |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=powo.science.kew.org}}</ref>

The species is found in terrestrial ecosystems, in habitats such as temperate forests and grasslands, Mediterranean-type shrublands, and rocky areas (e.g., inland cliffs and mountain peaks). <ref name="iucn" /> It can also be artificially found in pastures since it is sometimes cultivated as forage crops.<ref name="go botany" />

== Ecology ==
[[Thyme]], a dominant aromatic shrub, affects the competitive status of ''M. rigidula''. When ''M. rigidula'' is grown alone without a competitor, it tends to survive better in soil with thyme. ''M. rigidula'' grown on soil without thyme has a higher [[biomass]].<ref name="Journal of Ecology">{{cite journal |last1=Ehlers |first1=Bodil K. |last2=David |first2=Patrice |last3=Damgaard |first3=Christian F. |last4=Lenormand |first4=Thomas |title=Competitor relatedness, indirect soil effects and plant coexistence |journal=Journal of Ecology |date=July 2016 |volume=104 |issue=4 |pages=1126–1135 |doi=10.1111/1365-2745.12568 |s2cid=87409838 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2016JEcol.104.1126E }}</ref>

In laboratory bioassays and field experiments investigating the allelopathic and autotoxic effects of burclover residue on burclover and winter wheat seedlings, the results showed that soils treated with burclover leachates resulted in increased PO<sub>4</sub>–P, NH<sub>4</sub>–N, electrical conductivity, total [[Phenols|phenolic]] content, and decreased [[soil pH]]. The bioassay results also found that the full-strength leachate of burclover exhibited allelopathy effects on wheat, while growth inhibition of burclover seedlings in the field showed that burclover may have autotoxicity that could reduce productivity.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mbũgwa |first1=Gatua wa |last2=Krall |first2=James |last3=Legg |first3=David |title=Interferences of Tifton Burclover Residues with Growth of Burclover and Wheat Seedlings |journal=Agronomy Journal|date=1 July 2012 |volume=104 |issue=4 |pages=982–990 |doi=10.2134/agronj2012.0036 |bibcode=2012AgrJ..104..982M |url=https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2134/agronj2012.0036 |access-date=13 April 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Conservation ==
''M. rigidula'' is currently on the [[IUCN Red List]] as LC or least concern. It has a stable current population trend, and there are neither any extreme population fluctuations nor any extreme subpopulation fluctuations. The population is not severely fragmented and the mature individuals are not on a continuous decline. It is abundant in Turkey and has a stable global population trend but is a protected species in Hungary.<ref name="iucn" />

== Uses ==
[[Saponin|Saponins]] produced by ''Medicago'' species are being studied by pharmaceutical companies due to their effectiveness against fungal growth and tumorigenesis. They have also been found to be toxic to bacteria and certain viruses. ''M. rigidula'' plants were found to have higher concentrations of saponins when compared to other ''Medicago'' species. <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Guanzhen |last2=Wang |first2=Junlong |last3=Liu |first3=Wei |last4=Nisar |first4=Muhammad Farrukh |last5=El-Esawi |first5=Mohamed A. |last6=Wan |first6=Chunpeng |title=Biological Activities and Chemistry of Triterpene Saponins from Medicago Species: An Update Review |journal=Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine |date=26 May 2021 |volume=2021 |pages=1–11 |doi=10.1155/2021/6617916|pmid=34122600 |pmc=8172297 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Data has shown that ''M. rigidula'' can regenerate naturally and form productive pastures in rotation with wheat. Since it is able to tolerate the cold, it is a suitable annual legume that is adapted to the soils and climate of north Syria and the ley-farming system. The successful development of ''M. rigidula'' [[cultivars]] could aid livestock production in west Asia and north Africa.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Abd El-Moneim |first1=A. M. |last2=Cocks |first2=P. S. |title=Adaptation of Medicago rigidula to a cereal–pasture rotation in north-west Syria |journal=The Journal of Agricultural Science |date=27 March 2009 |volume=107 |issue=1 |pages=179–186 |doi=10.1017/S0021859600066934 |s2cid=84315446 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-agricultural-science/article/abs/adaptation-of-medicago-rigidula-to-a-cerealpasture-rotation-in-northwest-syria/DB6D2B92F8077A73600C49E224E21366 |access-date=13 April 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
